title: [sustainability] the sustainability line as the core metric set defines it: each north star's target beside its range (a general ranges-file "target"), U1 "<n> of <rows>" over the recovery table's rows, no range for U2 in its first week of judged data
prompt:
Spawn, objective 181 [sustainability] (after 185; the owner's core metric set of 2026-11-14 18:42, part (a), with the lead's rulings of 2026-11-14): the sustainability line as the set defines it. Each north star's target is shown beside its range. U1 is counted out of the recovery table's rows. U2 has no range in its first week of data.

The set's sustainability line has:
- NORTH STAR: human interventions per agent-hour, target under 0.1;
- U1: critical resources with a restore passed in 7 days (6 of 6);
- U2: "Needs you is right", its target to be proposed after a week of data.
The storage and performance north stars have targets too: 50 MB per landing and 20 min.
The card shows none of these targets. U1 reads as a bare count: it doesn't say how many resources there are, or which. U2 is judged against whatever range the file gives it, before there is a week of judged data to choose one from.

Base: 185 (n180 o185 834012c3, sync/obj-185), on 180 (o180 8c7d9cce), on 176 R2 (744b5311 on 007563ed). R1 was on 185 7985f84c (old history); moved by content, its +/- lines unchanged.

Read first:
- crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines.rs: `Ranges`, `parse_ranges`, `figure_json`, `answer`, `lines_at`;
- crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/drills.rs: `read`, `figures`;
- crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/observability.rs: `judged_share`;
- web/src/coreLines.ts: `mark`; web/src/components/aui/NorthStarChart.tsx.

What changes:
(1) Targets, one general change. A ranges file entry may give `"target": <number>`. `parse_ranges` keeps it in `Ranges.targets`, apart from the range.
   - An entry with a target alone gives no range, and is not left out.
   - The answer says it as the figure's `target`. It is never judged against: the state still comes from the range alone.
   - The card says "target <value in the unit's words>". For a north star, it follows the range in the footer.
   - The lead sets the three targets in core-lines.json after landing: storage 50 MB per landing, performance 20 min, sustainability 0.1.
(2) U1 (recoverability.restores_passed) is driven by the Core lines file's recovery rows, as the lead ruled. Live, these are the owner's six.
   - It says `of`, the row count; the card reads "<n> of <rows>".
   - Its note names the rows: "rows: <name>, ...".
   - What counts is unchanged: a pass within 7 days, with the newest drill not failed. A row with no drill reads "no drill" in the card's drill list and never counts.
   - Each row's last pass and its age stay in that list, as objectives 093 and 112 give them.
   - With no rows, there is neither `of` nor a note.
(3) U2 (observability.needs_you_right) gets `range_note`. While the note is set, the ranges file's range is not applied, so U2 is never out of range and raises no guardrail alert. Its week starts at its first judged value: the first hourly host.core_lines sample carrying it as a number.
   - Before any value: "range proposed 7 days after the first judged value".
   - With a value no sample carries yet: the week starts now.
   - During the week: "range proposed after <YYYY-MM-DD>", the week's end in UTC.
   - After the week: no note, and the file's range applies.
   The card says the note where the range would be. The store reads the first sample through `first_core_lines_value(key)` (host.rs).
   Figure gains `of` and `range_note`. Both are said only when set.

What stays as it is:
- every value;
- the ranges file's ranges, and the ranges that are left out (an entry with neither a bound nor a target is left out as before, with the same reason);
- the drill rows and how they are read;
- the alert step, which reads the answer's state as before.
The demoted figures already raise alerts when out of range (176's alert_figures; the live file has a range for all six), so 181 adds none.

Polled reads: `first_core_lines_value` runs on every /api/core-lines answer, the hourly sample and the guardrail alerts' readings. It reads the host.core_lines samples through their partial index (spawn_events_host_core_lines, on recorded_at_ms), oldest first, and stops at the first that carries the figure. Once a sample carries U2 the walk stops there; at worst, it walks every hourly sample, about 24 a day since objective 090. I have not read the live samples. Read-only timing on live:
  psql "$SPAWN_DATABASE_URL" -c "explain analyze select e.recorded_at_ms from spawn_events e where e.session_id = 'session_control' and e.event_name = 'control.recorded' and e.kind -> 'detail' -> 'record' ->> 'type' = 'host.core_lines' and jsonb_typeof(e.kind -> 'detail' -> 'record' -> 'values' -> 'observability.needs_you_right') = 'number' order by e.recorded_at_ms limit 1"
Expected under 5 ms; the lead times it.

Tests:
- serve/core_lines.rs: a_target_is_said_beside_the_figure_apart_from_its_range (new: target with a range, target alone, the answer's target, range and state);
- serve/core_lines/observability.rs: needs_you_is_right_takes_no_range_in_its_first_week_of_data (new: during the week, at its end, before any value, a value with no sample, and the held range never out);
- serve/core_lines/drills.rs: a few lines added to the existing drills test, for U1's `of` and note (each row named, rows without a drill among them; no rows, neither);
- crates/spawn-postgres/tests/storage.rs: the_first_sample_carrying_a_figure_is_found (new);
- web/test/coreLines.test.ts: "a target is said apart from the range, a count out of its rows, a held range by its note (objective 181)" (new).

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines.rs, crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/drills.rs, crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/observability.rs, crates/spawn-postgres/src/host.rs, crates/spawn-postgres/tests/storage.rs, web/src/coreLines.ts, web/src/components/aui/NorthStarChart.tsx, web/test/coreLines.test.ts. The owner's (181-owner.diff): rsi/scenarios/181.sh (new). Stacked on 185, which shares core_lines.rs, host.rs and tests/storage.rs.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/181.sh is a black box through `GET /api/core-lines`. The ranges file gives:
- the sustainability north star {"max": 0.1, "target": 0.1};
- the storage north star {"target": 52428800};
- U2 {"min": 0.8}.
The recovery table has three rows:
- Live database, record backup.verified, which passed an hour ago (seeded);
- Mission repositories, record backup.drilled.missions, never passed;
- Controllers, no drill.
(1) The sustainability north star says target 0.1 and range {"max": 0.1}. The storage north star says target 52428800 and range null. No entry is left out.
(2) U1 is 1 of 3, its note "rows: Live database, Mission repositories, Controllers".
(3) U2's range and range_note go through three stages:
   - with no sample: range null, note "range proposed 7 days after the first judged value";
   - with its first sample two days ago: range null, note "range proposed after <today + 5 days>";
   - with its first sample eight days ago: range {"min": 0.8}, and no note.
On the base (185), 181.sh exits 1: "(1) the sustainability north star's target and range: expected [[0.1,{\"max\":0.1}]], got [[null,{\"max\":0.1}]]", "(1) the storage north star's target alone: expected [[52428800,null]], got [[null,null]]", "(1) entries left out: expected [[]], got [[\"storage.bytes_per_landing\"]]", "(2) U1: passed in 7 days, out of the rows: expected [[1,3]], got [[1,null]]" (the runner prints the first four).

14 mutants (mut181.py), each alone, all killed:
- the 11 in the crates, each its own binary, each by 181.sh: target-not-read, target-alone-ignored, target-not-said, target-as-range, of-dropped, rows-note-dropped, range-note-ignored, week-never-ends, unjudged-no-note, first-any-sample, u2-not-wired. All but u2-not-wired are also failed by a unit or store test.
- the 3 in web/src (web-of-dropped, web-range-note-dropped, web-target-dropped), by the new web test. The runner runs no web tests, so these ran by hand: web181.sh (in this folder), its output in the proof.
